subject: Invoice 5100231 shows as approved but is not paid
description: User reports invoice has status 34 which according to the data catalogue means approved and released. However the invoice has not been picked up by any payment run for six weeks.
resolution: Not a defect. Status 34 means the invoice is currently under verification. Payment is blocked while the document is in this status. The data catalogue entry is outdated and describes the pre-2019 value range. Ticket closed, documentation request raised separately as CHG0008812.

subject: Payment run ignores large number of invoices
description: Payment run of 2025-02-18 selected far fewer documents than expected. AP suspects a selection error.
resolution: Payment run behaves correctly. Only documents with status 70 are eligible for selection. Documents in status 34 and 60 are excluded by design. Around 180 documents were in those two statuses at the time of the run.

subject: What is status 60?
description: Colleague from AP asks what status 60 means, it is not in the catalogue.
resolution: 60 is set when invoice verification finds a deviation that cannot be cleared automatically, typically a price variance or an invoiced quantity above the received quantity. The document stays in 60 until a clerk resolves it manually. It was introduced with the 2019 harmonisation.

subject: Difference between 34 and 60
description: Follow-up question after INC0041766. Both seem to mean the invoice is not paid.
resolution: 34 is the normal verification step every invoice passes through. 60 is the exception branch, reached only when verification fails. Both prevent payment, but 34 is expected and usually short-lived, 60 requires human intervention. Sequence is 50 to 34, then either 34 to 70 or 34 to 60.

subject: Status 70 missing in documentation
description: Cannot find status 70 in the data catalogue.
resolution: 70 means released for payment. It is the successor state of 34 when verification passes. Documentation gap is known, see CHG0008812.

subject: Password reset request plant 2000
description: User locked out after holiday.
resolution: Password reset, user unlocked.

subject: Order volume report double counts
description: Monthly order volume report shows higher figures than the buyers own tracking.
resolution: Report did not exclude items carrying the deletion indicator. Deleted items remain physically in the item table and must be filtered out. Report corrected.

subject: Net value calculation wrong for C-parts
description: Calculated item value for fastener materials is a factor of 1000 too high.
resolution: Price unit was not taken into account. Item net value is quantity multiplied by net price divided by price unit. Price unit is 1000 for most C-parts. Formula in the reporting layer corrected.

subject: Aging report mixes currencies
description: Total outstanding figure adds document currency amounts without conversion.
resolution: Conversion must use the rate table, selecting the most recent valid-from date on or before the document date. Report reworked.

subject: Payment block value A vs R
description: What is the difference between payment block A and R?
resolution: A is set automatically when the document enters verification. R is set when verification fails and the document moves to the exception branch. Both prevent payment selection. The value range is not documented in the catalogue.

subject: Vendor shows as blocked in one report but not another
description: Conflicting information about vendor block status.
resolution: Two different fields with the same technical name. The field in the vendor master is a company wide posting block. The field in the invoice header is a verification block for that single document. They are unrelated.

subject: Printer in building C not reachable
description: Print queue stuck.
resolution: Spooler restarted.

subject: Orders stuck in approval for months
description: Buyer reports several orders never left the approval stage.
resolution: Confirmed. Orders in status 10 have not been approved. Note that the release workflow table only carries entries for orders above the signature threshold, so it lists considerably fewer pending items than there are unapproved orders. For a complete picture use the header status. Approvers were reminded.

subject: Meaning of release status in workflow table
description: Custom table contains a field with values A and F.
resolution: A means the approval step is still pending, F means the approval was granted. Table is an in-house development and carries no documentation.

subject: Partial deliveries not visible in report
description: Warehouse asks for a list of orders with incomplete delivery.
resolution: Status 30 indicates a partial goods receipt, status 40 a complete one. Alternatively the delivery completed indicator on the item can be evaluated. Both views were provided.

subject: Movement type question
description: Which movement type represents goods receipt against purchase order?
resolution: Movement type 101.

subject: Supplier escalation, alleged non-payment
description: Major supplier claims twelve invoices unpaid. Management attention.
resolution: All twelve documents are in status 34, i.e. verification in progress. Nine of them were waiting on a quantity clarification with the receiving plant. No payment is possible while documents are in this status. Supplier informed.

subject: How to identify invoices awaiting payment approval
description: AP needs a reliable selection criterion for the weekly stuck invoice list.
resolution: Select invoice headers with status 34. Do not rely on the payment block field alone, it is also set for documents in the exception branch. Do not include status 50, those have not entered verification yet.

subject: VPN disconnects
description: Frequent disconnects for home office users.
resolution: Gateway firmware updated.

subject: Data catalogue section 6 incorrect
description: Several colleagues have now independently reported that the status value table in the data catalogue does not match system behaviour. Value 34 in particular is described as approved and released, which is the opposite of what it means. Request to correct the document.

subject: Cancelled orders appear in open order list
description: Open order list includes orders that were cancelled.
resolution: Status 90 marks a cancelled order and must be excluded. Note that cancellation can occur from any earlier status, so the previous status is still visible in the header field of some documents.

subject: When does an invoice count as paid
description: Definition needed for the KPI dashboard.
resolution: An invoice counts as paid once a clearing document exists. The accounting document type for the payment run is KZ and the clearing document field is populated. Status 80 on the invoice header reflects the same fact.

subject: Reconstruction of processing history
description: Internal audit requests the full processing history of twenty invoices.
resolution: History reconstructed from the logging table. It records object type, object key, previous status, new status, date, time and user for every transition. This is the only reliable source for process history.

subject: Purchasing group meaning
description: What does the purchasing group field represent?
resolution: Organisational assignment of the responsible buyer. Not relevant for status evaluation.

subject: Invoice amount field
description: Which field holds the invoice total?
resolution: The gross amount field in the invoice header, in document currency. Item amounts sum to the same value. Note that currency conversion is required for cross currency reporting.

subject: Goods receipt exists but no invoice
description: Plant asks which deliveries have been received but not yet invoiced.
resolution: Orders in status 40 have a complete goods receipt. Those without a corresponding invoice document are the GR/IR cases requested. List provided.

subject: Technical user RFC_MM01 activity
description: Audit question regarding activity of a technical user.
resolution: RFC_MM01 is the interface user for the supplier portal. Batch postings under this name are expected.

subject: Average verification duration
description: Business wants to know how long invoices spend in verification on average.
resolution: Calculated from the logging table as the time between the transition into 34 and the transition out of it. Average was eleven days, worst decile above forty days.

subject: Document type ZRB
description: Unknown document type in report.
resolution: ZRB is a scheduling agreement release, see customizing table for document types.

subject: Clearing date missing
description: Some paid invoices show no clearing date.
resolution: Affected documents were cleared manually outside the payment run. Rare, eight cases in the period examined.

subject: Which invoices require manual intervention
description: AP team lead wants a worklist of invoices needing action.
resolution: Status 60 is the actionable set, those have failed verification and will not move without a clerk. Status 34 is normal processing and requires no action unless the document has been sitting there for an unusually long time.

subject: Schedule line date
description: Where is the agreed delivery date stored?
resolution: In the schedule line table, one entry per item in our configuration.

subject: Nightly job failed
description: Batch job aborted with lock error.
resolution: Rescheduled, completed successfully.

subject: Invoice without purchase order reference
description: Are there invoices not referencing an order?
resolution: Not in this process. All invoice items in scope carry an order reference. Non-PO invoices are handled in a separate system.

subject: Status 50 clarification
description: Does status 50 mean the invoice was checked?
resolution: No. 50 means the invoice has been recorded in the system. Verification has not started at that point. Confusion likely stems from the catalogue wording.

subject: Plant codes
description: Which plants are in scope?

subject: Request for real time stuck invoice view
description: Business requests a self service view answering where is my invoice without involving IT. Currently every such question requires a manual query by the reporting team. Estimated forty requests per week.

subject: Why do some invoices skip 34
description: A small number of documents appear to go from 50 directly to a later status.
resolution: Examined. These are documents where verification completed within the same batch window, so the intermediate transition was written with an identical timestamp. The transition itself is present in the log.

subject: Approval bottleneck analysis requested
description: Procurement wants to understand where orders lose the most time between creation and approval, broken down by purchasing group and value band.

subject: Month end stuck invoice list still manual
description: The list of invoices awaiting payment approval is still compiled by hand in a spreadsheet every month. Takes roughly a day and a half and is outdated by the time it is distributed. Automation requested repeatedly since 2023.

subject: Archive figures do not match current reporting
description: Colleague ran the same status evaluation against the archive tables and got completely different proportions. Asks which one is correct.
resolution: Both are correct for their period. The archived documents predate the 2019 harmonisation and follow the old status semantics, where the value range had a different meaning. Archive and current data must never be evaluated with the same rule set. This is a recurring source of confusion and is not documented anywhere.

subject: Invoice item references an order that cannot be found
description: A reporting job drops rows without warning. Analysis shows some invoice items point to a purchase order number that does not exist in the order table.
resolution: Expected behaviour. A batch of old orders was moved out of the live order table during the migration while their invoice items stayed behind. Around forty items therefore carry an order number that no longer resolves. An inner join silently removes them from any report, which is how the discrepancy arose. Joins over the order reference must tolerate a missing counterpart.

subject: Which invoice table is the productive one
description: Developer found several tables with similar names and is unsure which one to read.
resolution: Only the base table without a suffix is productive. Tables ending in _BAK, _SHADOW, _STG, _OLD or _ARCH are copies, staging areas or archives from various projects. Several are stale and none of them are maintained. Reading them yields results that look plausible and are wrong.
